gen-gf-oxanium-gf-duru-sans: Oxanium draws every letter with one unbroken line of constant weight, giving the headline a machined, confident look. Duru Sans fills its lines with wide-open small letters and barely-there ascenders, so paragraphs read smooth and low-slung.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-fresca: Fresca keeps its strokes free of calligraphic thinning, with short ascenders over big bowls that stay open to the outside. And Oxanium handles the loud part, its tall lowercase and monoline curves doing the attention-grabbing while the plain sans just talks.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-funnel-sans: Funnel Sans holds its stroke widths steady from stem to curve, with an e that opens like a pried clasp and ascenders just above the x-height. Oxanium is the one with swagger, while this sans-serif does the quiet work.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-gafata: Uninterrupted monoline strokes give Oxanium a look like cut wire, with curves that finish in clear daylight and tall lowercase. Gafata follows with a wide-eyed e and short stalks, so a long passage goes down easily.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-geist: Geist keeps a quiet, level beat with no accents of weight, so words land as solid blocks rather than skylines. But Oxanium is the showpiece here, its monoline strokes and big lowercase carrying the attitude that the sans-serif declines to.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-georama: Georama reads friendly and unfussy, its c pulled open like a bracelet and its capitals barely rising. Oxanium sets thin-looking monoline letters with no thinner parts above that, and the display attitude against the plain sans keeps the page lively.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-gidole: Gidole reads as though drawn in neon tube, every stroke the same, with terminals parted like open scissor blades. Yet Oxanium brings the swagger on top, its big lowercase and monoline curves giving the plain sans something to stand beside.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-golos-text: Golos Text fills the line with a tall x-height and a widely parted s, every letter built from one width of stroke. Oxanium sits on top with a commanding display voice, so keep Golos Text comfortably large and it will hold up.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-hedvig-letters-sans: Sharp, wiry and unmistakably techy, Oxanium keeps one monoline stroke throughout, while Hedvig Letters Sans leaves a wide gap where the c ends. Oxanium shouts best; the sans-serif speaks best, with small letters nearly as tall as capitals.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-heebo: Cut-ribbon lines, all one width, make Oxanium look crisp and slightly futuristic. Heebo gives the text a tall central band and curves that stop short, so shrinking the heading or enlarging the sans would blur who leads.
